'''Gantt:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Jesse Helms]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Jesse Helms]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNC}} The '''North Carolina United States Senate election of 1996''' was held on November 5, 1996 as part of the [[1996 United States Senate elections|nationwide elections to the Senate]], and coincided with the [[1996 United States presidential election|1996 presidential election]]. The general election was a rematch of the [[1990 United States Senate election in North Carolina|1990 election]] between [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Jesse Helms]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Harvey Gantt]], the former [[Mayor of Charlotte, North Carolina|Mayor of Charlotte]]. Helms won re-election to a fifth and final term by a slightly wider margin than in 1990. Helms would ultimately tie with [[Furnifold Simmons]] as North Carolina's longest-serving U.S senator, with a record of 30 years. ==Democratic primary== In the Democratic primary, Gantt defeated Charles Sanders, who was CEO of pharmaceutical company [[GlaxoSmithKline|Glaxo]].{{Cite web|first=JAY |last=EUBANK |title=CHARGE!: CHARLES SANDERS TURNS HIS ENERGY TO POLITICS|url=https://greensboro.com/charge-charles-sanders-turns-his-energy-to-politics/article_050cb66e-dddb-54d2-917e-4460e8455700.html|access-date=2022-02-13|website=Greensboro News and Record|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Gantt Beats Sanders in N.C. Senate Primary, Setting Up Helms Rematch|url=https://apnews.com/article/5a9f9097dc447c318307abb25eb786aa|access-date=2022-02-13|website=AP NEWS|language=en}} As a candidate, Gantt supported a [[Balanced budget amendment|balanced federal budget]], a $10,000 tax deduction for the middle-class, while also pledging to defend Medicare and education funding.{{Cite web|title=AllPolitics - North Carolina Senate Race - Nov. 5, 1996|url=https://www.cnn.com/ALLPOLITICS/1996/news/9611/05/senate/nc/|access-date=2022-02-13|website=www.cnn.com}}{{Election box begin | title = 1996 North Carolina U.S. Senate Democratic primary election{{cite web | title=North Carolina DataNet #46 | url=http://southnow.org/southnow-publications/nc-datanet/DataNet%20April08.pdf | date=April 2008 | publisher=[[University of North Carolina]] | access-date=June 12, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080725034758/http://southnow.org/southnow-publications/nc-datanet/DataNet%20April08.pdf | archive-date=July 25, 2008 | df=mdy-all }}}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = [[Harvey Gantt]] | votes = 308,337 | percentage = 52.40% | change = +14.88% }} {{Election box candidate with party link | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = Charles Sanders | votes = 245,297 | percentage = 41.68% | change = N/A }} {{Election box candidate with party link | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = Ralph McKinney | votes = 34,829 | percentage = 5.92% | change = N/A }} {{Election box turnout | votes = 588,463 | percentage = | change = }} {{Election box end}} ==Republican primary== Jesse Helms won the Republican Party's nomination unopposed. ==General election== During the campaign, Helms refused to debate Gantt or appear in public with him, instead choosing to focus his campaign's energy on television advertisements. Helms' campaign ads accused Gantt of being too socially liberal on issues such as [[LGBT rights in the United States|gay rights]] and the [[Capital punishment|death penalty]]. A major issue in the campaign were proposals for [[Tobacco in the United States|tobacco regulation]]: Helms accused Gantt of supporting President [[Bill Clinton]]'s efforts to regulate tobacco use, while Gantt broke with his party to criticize Clinton on the subject. In return, Gantt accused Helms of being out-of-touch on "kitchen table issues" affecting working-class families, and stated that Helms "appeals to the bigotry and the prejudice that may be within all of us", though stopped short of calling Helms a racist.{{Cite news|last=Grove|first=Lloyd|date=1996-05-24|title=THE BALLOT OF HARVEY GANTT|language=en-US|newspaper=Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1996/05/24/the-ballot-of-harvey-gantt/86fc5150-ceaa-4ee8-b2ec-ebfc5e019041/|access-date=2022-02-13|issn=0190-8286}} === Results === Following
